items.title: 11 Medicare Advantage Insurers Sue CMS Over 2027 Star Ratings and Nearly $4 Billion in Payments - Medical Daily
items.reason: This reports litigation by multiple Medicare Advantage insurers (payers) against CMS involving Star Ratings methodology and $4 billion in payment disputes, which directly falls under payer litigation and CMS enforcement/sanctions.
items.summary: Eleven Medicare Advantage insurers have filed a lawsuit against CMS challenging the 2027 Star Ratings methodology and disputing approximately $4 billion in related payments. The suit contests CMS's approach to calculating Star Ratings, which determine MA plan quality scores and affect bonus payments to insurers. The litigation involves major payers operating in the Medicare Advantage market and directly impacts payment obligations and quality-metric incentives. For revenue-cycle teams, this case matters because Star Rating disputes can affect overall payer solvency, claims-payment capacity, and negotiating leverage with health plans, particularly if CMS enforcement or payment adjustments result from the litigation outcome.

items.title: Long-term care group sues Aetna over prior authorization denials associated with hospital transfers - HealthExec
items.reason: This item reports a lawsuit against Aetna (a major payer) involving claims-denial practices (prior authorization denials), which directly falls within the payer litigation and enforcement topic.
items.summary: A long-term care group has filed a lawsuit against Aetna alleging improper denial of prior authorization requests related to hospital transfers. The suit challenges Aetna's prior authorization practices in the context of patient transitions from long-term care facilities to hospitals. This litigation is relevant to revenue-cycle teams as prior authorization denials and claims-denial disputes are common sources of payment delays and revenue loss, and the outcome may affect how payers process transfer-related authorization requests across the industry.
